title: Cannabis and Stroke: A 37% Signal Across 100 Million People
hook: The largest analysis yet ties recreational drug use to stroke — cocaine nearly doubling risk, amphetamines more than doubling it, and cannabis up 37%, including in young adults.
key_points: An analysis pooling data on more than 100 million people examined recreational drug use and stroke.
Cannabis use was associated with a 37% higher risk of stroke.
Cocaine was linked to nearly double the risk; amphetamines to more than double.
The association held among younger adults — the group least likely to expect a stroke.
Smoking cannabis raises blood pressure and heart rate acutely, a plausible route to stroke.
Observational data: association, not proof of causation, and dose details vary across studies.
content_html: Pooling data on more than 100 million people, researchers report consistent links between recreational drug use and stroke. Cocaine was associated with nearly double the risk. Amphetamines, more than double. Cannabis — the one most users consider benign — with a 37% increase.
extra_html:
The part worth sitting with is the age distribution: the associations showed up among younger adults, who almost never consider stroke a personal risk. That's the group for whom this changes anything. The mechanisms aren't mysterious either — smoking cannabis acutely raises heart rate and blood pressure and stresses blood vessels, which is the same general route by which stimulants are thought to trigger strokes.

Read the numbers as associations, not verdicts. Pooled observational data carries the usual confounders — tobacco use often travels with cannabis, and study definitions of "use" vary from occasional to daily. But a 37% relative increase on a low baseline risk is still small in absolute terms for a healthy 25-year-old, and considerably less small for someone with high blood pressure, a clotting disorder, or a family history of stroke. That's the conversation this finding actually belongs in.

related.title: Heavy Marijuana Smoking and Cancer Risk
related.hook: Growing research links heavy marijuana smoking to a higher risk of lung and head-and-neck cancers — though scientists still don't know how much use is enough to meaningfully raise that risk.

related.title: Cannabis for Stress May Disrupt the Stress System
related.hook: Frequent cannabis users woke up with cortisol already elevated — raising the possibility that using it to relax gradually dysregulates the system that handles stress.

related.title: Teen Cannabis Use and Serious Mental Illness
related.hook: A study of more than 463,000 adolescents tied teen cannabis use to roughly double the risk of serious mental illness — and the use usually came first.

related.title: The Real Cause of a Common Stroke May Have Been Missed for Decades
related.hook: A common type of stroke may not be mainly caused by fatty plaque after all — the strongest link was found with damaged small blood vessels deep in the brain.

related.title: Understanding Blood Pressure
related.hook: High blood pressure is called the 'silent killer' for a reason — it usually has no symptoms, yet it quietly raises your risk of heart attack and stroke.

flashcards.prompt: Which drug in this analysis carried the largest stroke association?

choices.text: Amphetamines — more than double the risk

flashcards.explanation_html: Amphetamines were linked to more than double the risk, cocaine to nearly double, and cannabis to a 37% increase. All three pointed the same direction; the magnitudes differ a lot.

flashcards.prompt: Why is the finding in younger adults especially notable?
flashcards.back_html: Stroke is usually framed as an older person's risk, so young users don't factor it in at all. The association held in this group — meaning the risk isn't confined to people who already have age-related vascular disease.

flashcards.prompt: What's a plausible mechanism for cannabis raising stroke risk?
flashcards.back_html: Smoking it acutely raises blood pressure and heart rate, and stresses blood vessels — the same pathways through which other stimulants are thought to trigger strokes.
